_comment: MCP connectors, as data. Copy to config/connectors.json and edit; that file is gitignored.
This example is also the fallback, so the app runs with no real file present.
url       a streamable-http MCP endpoint. Everything here is dialled directly —
these are ordinary HTTP services and never needed a broker in front of them.
requires  environment variables that must be non-empty for the connector to work.
A connector missing its credential is reported as 'unconfigured', not 'down':
one needs a key added, the other needs a service restarted.
auth      bearer token or explicit headers. ${VAR} is substituted from the environment
at load time, so no secret is ever written into this file.
enabled   set false to keep an entry documented but out of the running set.

connectors.name: bright-data
connectors.description: Paid, unmetered scraping. The escape hatch for pages a plain fetch cannot read — Reddit, and anything behind a bot check. Never tried first, because it is metered.

connectors.name: brave
connectors.description: Brave web, news, video and image search. Note the free tier is one request per second and 429s anything faster — app/server/search.ts serialises every call in the process for exactly this reason.

connectors.name: youtube
connectors.description: YouTube search over videos, channels and playlists, with view/like/comment counts and publish dates. The primary feed source, and the fastest to answer.

connectors.name: x
connectors.description: X (Twitter): posts and their likers/reposters/quoters, full-archive search, user timelines and mentions, trends.

connectors.name: tiktok
connectors.description: TikTok keyword search plus a video's full metadata and captions/transcript.

connectors.name: hn
connectors.description: Hacker News stories, full comment threads and user profiles. Largely redundant now: a plain fetch of an HN item page already yields every comment, so app/server/content.ts reads threads without going through here.

connectors.name: reddit
connectors.description: Reddit. Disabled: Reddit blocks unauthenticated requests from this network on every route tried, so the connector reports up and returns nothing. Reddit is reached through bright-data instead.

connectors.name: exa
connectors.description: Exa neural search. Disabled: the shared endpoint returned empty results and 429s for a full day, and a broken connector wired into every stage just makes turns fail and panels come back blank.

connectors.name: discord
connectors.description: Discord bot control: channels, messages, reactions, roles, moderation, webhooks, forums and invites. The bot token lives in the container, which is bound to loopback, so no auth block here.

connectors.name: linkedin
connectors.description: LinkedIn through a logged-in browser session: profiles, company pages and post search. The session lives in the container's own browser profile, so there is no credential here to check — if it is logged out, the probe is what tells you.

connectors.name: telegram
connectors.description: Telegram as your own account: chats, groups, contacts, messages, folders and media.

connectors.name: signal
connectors.description: Signal via a registered signal-cli number: send and receive direct and group messages.

connectors.name: whatsapp
connectors.description: WhatsApp through a linked phone: contacts, chat history, sending messages and media.

connectors.name: instagram
connectors.description: The company's own Instagram Business account: profile, recent posts and their insights, connected pages, DMs. Manages an owned account rather than searching.

_roles: roles  what a connector is FOR, and therefore where the pipeline uses it:
search   discovery, the feed and the abuse sweep query it
scrape   reading a page a plain fetch cannot
contact  replying to whoever reported a defect (nothing sends yet — outbox only)
ticket   filing a defect and appending each loop step to it
exec     an isolated place to run a patched checkout's tests (Daytona, Docker, ...)
A list: bright-data really is both a search engine and a scraper.
bindings  which tool serves each role, and what its argument is called. Bound once,
visibly, rather than guessed per call — tool names are not standardised
(search_engine / tavily-search / web_search) and neither are argument names
(query / q / keyword). A role with no binding is declared but not used.
The settings screen suggests both by reading the server's own tools/list.
